excluded_seen: Steps 4d and 4e (examples/scale-up-closure-territories): these two worlds on side 1,024 to generation 4,096 from starts 15001 to 15008 and 16001 to 16108, read through blocks of 4 to 32. Blocks of 32 were read there at ages that do not match (generations 64 to 4,096), never at 4,096 to 16,384.

The sizing look (sizing.py here, exploratory): the first look's kept runs at matched ages, blocks of 4, 8 and 16, with the rule from the rung below run on. Every bound here was drawn from it and from step 4e's records. It ran nothing.
The search (examples/scale-up-search) ran both worlds on side 1,024 to generation 2,048 and read them by their correlation area.
Neither world has been run on side 2,048, or past generation 4,096 on a grid this large or larger, and no start from 18001 on has been generated or run.
body.not_tested: A claim about a rule run on through blocks of some size is not tested where more than 0.2 of neighbouring blocks of that size have different leaders when the rule is started (territories under five blocks across), on the world's trial starts; and no claim is tested without a number to judge.

C, the new rung.drawn from: a rung's own rule, learned at its matched age and run on over it: 0.62 and 0.53 of the changed blocks amiss at blocks of 8 and 16 in the still world, 0.51 and 0.50 in the busy one; 0.83 to 0.91 of the walls kept. With other draws these move by 0.02 or so.

G, the gap.drawn from: the gap at blocks of 16 at matched ages: 2.6% and 2.5% in the first look's runs, and by step 4e's registered ratio about 2.6% and 3.4% on its fresh starts. At blocks of 8 it was 8.7% and 5.7%. What it is at blocks of 32 nobody has seen: the claim there is only that it is smaller than at 16.

H, the chances.drawn from: the chance of changing hands at five rival neighbours at matched ages: 0.310, 0.238, 0.200 at blocks of 4, 8, 16 in the still world (each 0.77 and 0.84 of the one before), 0.296, 0.257, 0.224 in the busy one (0.87 and 0.87).

L, the ladder's own test.drawn from: the rule of the rung below run on at the rung above: 0.72 and 0.62 of the changed blocks amiss at blocks of 8 and 16 in the still world (1.16 and 1.18 times the rung's own rule), 0.54 and 0.53 in the busy one (1.05 and 1.07). With other draws the still world's gave 0.75 and 0.63 (1.25 and 1.16 times).

S, the same picture.drawn from: the walls at the start of each rung's matched age on side 1,024, in the first look's runs and step 4e's: 0.167, 0.175 and 0.170 at blocks of 8, 16 and 32 in the still world, 0.164, 0.162 and 0.166 in the busy one. They are within 5% of each other.

X, another grid.drawn from: step 4e's anchor: the first look's rule on fresh starts was within 0.03% of a rule learned from them. The grid here is twice as wide, and step 4's pair gave 0.02% across that step.

body.source: docs/scale-up-plan.md, steps 4d and 4e and decision D11
body.statement: Two worlds of territories are read through blocks of 4, 8, 16 and 32, each block on the square clock over the generations that match it, on a grid twice as wide as before run four times as long. At matched ages the world is the same picture at every rung (S); the rule learned on the smaller grid serves on the larger (X); the rule from the rung below is as far from the rung's own at blocks of 16 as it was, and nearer at blocks of 32 (G); the chance of changing hands levels off (H); at the new rung a world's own rule keeps the world (C); and the rule from the rung below, used as this rung's rule, runs the world on nearly as well as the rung's own (L).
body.title: Does the ladder come to a fixed point? One more rung.
